newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas moves higher on colder weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas moves higher on colder weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices edged higher Wednesday as colder weather approaching the northeastern and midwestern U.S. pumped up heating demand, market sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices gained about four cents to the low-$1.90s per mmBtu, with Henry Hub quoted mostly in the mid-$1.90s.
In south Texas, prices also edged up four cents to the high-$1.80s as storage buying continued and terrential rains pounded the region.
In the East, New York city-gate prices were steady to higher in the low-to-mid $2.20s, as forecasters called for colder temperatures in the region.
In the Midcontinent, prices climbed into the mid-$1.80s, up about five cents to about $1.85, with Demarcation quoted mostly at $1.85-1.87.
Temperatures in the Midwest are expected to run near to slightly above normal through early Friday but then turn colder for the weekend.

In the Permian basin, gas prices were up six cents to the high-$1.70s to low-$1.80s. Southern California border prices jumped into the high-$1.80s as West Coast continued to demand large volumes of gas to meet air-conditioning demand.
The 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in southern California is still expected to restart around March 20 following repairs of a leak, Edison International said.
According to a Reuter poll, withdrawal estimates for American Gas Association's storage report range mostly from 55 to 65 bcf, compared with 118 bcf a year ago.
